title: Test that a grab bar is secure and file the report
instruction: Grip the grab bar and pull it along its axis to test whether it is secure, then file the report tag on the pad matching what you found.
context: A grab bar that pulls out of its mounts fails exactly when a person's weight depends on it; NSPIRE inspectors check every grab bar by gripping and pulling it.
setup: A 12 cm long square steel grab bar (16 x 11 mm section, 50 g) rides two guide rails on a low base plate at the table's back. In the secure condition raised end stops capture the bar between the rails; in the loose condition the stops are absent. A white report tag (3 cm cube, 60 g) rests at the table front between a green pad (bar holds) and a yellow pad (bar pulls loose).
scoring: 1.0 for the tag filed on the pad matching the bar's actual condition (tag centre within 2.5 cm of the pad centre); 0.3 on the wrong pad (a report was filed but the test was misread); 0.0 if the tag is left anywhere else. Do-nothing: 0.
reset_notes: FAULT_MODE env var seeds the condition: 'secure' (stops present) or 'loose' (stops absent). Nothing is consumed; the bar is free to slide and the tag to be carried.
fidelity: The bar's wall mounts are a bench-top rail fixture at grasp height; a loose bar slides out of its rails rather than rotating in a stripped bracket. The bar is square-section (real bars are round) because that is what these 1 N fingertips hold. The scripted 3 cm pull slides a loose bar fully out of its rails while a capped bar does not move.
